1.headline: America Plans New Taxes on Goods From China
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
America wants new taxes on things from other countries.
On Wednesday, the United States made a new plan. It wants a new tax on goods from China. The tax is 20 percent. This kind of tax is called a tariff.
The plan is not only for China. Goods from Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and the European Union may cost more, too. In all, fourteen trading partners are on the list.
Why? The United States says these countries help their factories with money. So the factories make too many cheap things.
This is only a plan now. But it can change prices in many countries.
Again, the United States plans new tariffs on China, South Korea and others. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
미국이 다른 나라에서 오는 물건에 새 세금을 매기려고 합니다.
수요일에 미국이 새 계획을 내놓았습니다. 중국에서 오는 상품에 새 세금을 매기려는 것입니다. 세금은 20퍼센트입니다. 이런 세금을 관세라고 합니다.
이 계획은 중국만을 위한 것이 아닙니다. 일본, 한국, 대만, 유럽연합에서 오는 상품도 더 비싸질 수 있습니다. 모두 합쳐 14개 교역 상대가 목록에 올라 있습니다.
왜일까요? 미국은 이 나라들이 돈으로 자기 나라 공장을 돕는다고 말합니다. 그래서 공장들이 싼 물건을 너무 많이 만든다는 것입니다.
지금은 계획일 뿐입니다. 하지만 많은 나라의 물가를 바꿀 수 있습니다.
다시 말해, 미국이 중국과 한국 등에 새 관세를 매길 계획입니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: US Plans New Tariffs on China, South Korea and Others
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Will things from China and South Korea soon cost more in America?

On Wednesday, the Trump administration shared a plan for new tariffs. A tariff is a tax on goods from another country. Goods from China would get an extra 20 percent tariff. Import taxes would also go up for the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other trading partners.

Why? Officials say these places give money to their factories. Because of this, the factories make too many cheap products. There is one more reason. In February, the Supreme Court said the president could not use an emergency to put tariffs on almost everything. The new plan uses a different law.
Officials say these are only proposals for now. A proposal is an idea that is not final yet.

This news matters because America buys goods from all over the world. New tariffs can change prices and business plans in many countries. Also, a short trade peace between America and China ends on January 10.
To sum up, the United States plans new tariffs on China, South Korea and many other partners.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
중국과 한국에서 온 물건이 곧 미국에서 더 비싸질까요?
수요일에 트럼프 행정부가 새 관세 계획을 내놓았습니다. 관세는 다른 나라에서 들어오는 상품에 매기는 세금입니다. 중국산 상품에는 20퍼센트의 관세가 추가로 붙게 됩니다. 유럽연합, 일본, 한국, 대만과 다른 교역 상대 9곳에 대한 수입 관세도 오르게 됩니다.
왜일까요? 관리들은 이 나라들이 자국 공장에 돈을 준다고 말합니다. 그 때문에 공장들이 값싼 제품을 너무 많이 만든다는 것입니다. 이유가 하나 더 있습니다. 2월에 대법원은 대통령이 비상사태를 이유로 거의 모든 물건에 관세를 매길 수는 없다고 판단했습니다. 새 계획은 다른 법을 사용합니다.
관리들은 이것이 지금은 제안일 뿐이라고 말합니다. 제안이란 아직 최종 결정이 아닌 생각을 말합니다.
이 소식이 중요한 이유는 미국이 전 세계에서 상품을 사들이기 때문입니다. 새 관세는 여러 나라의 물가와 사업 계획을 바꿀 수 있습니다. 또 미국과 중국 사이의 짧은 무역 휴전이 1월 10일에 끝납니다.
정리하면, 미국은 중국과 한국을 비롯한 많은 교역 상대에 새 관세를 매길 계획입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: US Plans New Tariffs on China, South Korea and Many Others
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
The United States wants to make many imported goods more expensive, and South Korea is on the list.

On Wednesday, the Trump administration announced plans for new tariffs. A tariff is a tax on goods that come from another country. According to news reports, goods from China would face an extra 20 percent tariff. Some Chinese products could face a total of 45 percent. The plan also raises import taxes on the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other trading partners.

Why is the US doing this? Officials say these countries use subsidies, which means government money that helps factories. They say this lets factories make too many cheap products. There is another reason, too. In February, the Supreme Court ruled that the president could not use an economic emergency to put tariffs on almost everything. The new plan uses a different law from 1974, and it would bring back some of the lost money.
Brazil is also a target. The plan includes higher taxes on sugar and a new 10 percent tariff on airplanes. An official said these are only proposals for now, with no strict timeline.

Why does this matter? The US buys goods from all over the world, so its tariffs can change prices and business plans in many countries. A trade truce between the US and China ends on January 10. A truce means both sides agree to stop fighting for a while. President Trump met China's leader, Xi Jinping, last week, and he plans to host Xi at a G20 meeting in Florida next month.
To sum up, the United States plans new tariffs on China, South Korea and many other trading partners.
Thank you for listening.

미국이 여러 수입품을 더 비싸게 만들려고 하는데, 한국도 그 목록에 들어 있습니다.

미국은 왜 이렇게 할까요? 관리들은 이 나라들이 보조금, 즉 공장을 돕는 정부 돈을 쓴다고 말합니다. 그 결과 공장들이 값싼 제품을 너무 많이 만든다는 것입니다. 이유가 또 있습니다. 2월에 대법원은 대통령이 경제 비상사태를 이유로 거의 모든 물건에 관세를 매길 수는 없다고 판결했습니다. 새 계획은 1974년에 만든 다른 법을 사용하며, 잃어버린 수입 일부를 되찾게 됩니다.

정리하면, 미국은 중국과 한국을 비롯한 많은 교역 상대에 새 관세를 매길 계획입니다.

4.headline: Washington Proposes New Tariffs on China and 13 Other Partners
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Washington is preparing a new round of tariffs, and South Korea is among the economies on the list.

According to the Associated Press, the Trump administration on Wednesday proposed an additional 20 percent tariff on Chinese goods, which would bring the total duty on some Chinese products to 45 percent. It also plans higher import taxes on the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other major trading partners.

Officials say the measures target excess manufacturing driven by government subsidies and trade barriers. The tariffs are also meant to replace revenue lost after the Supreme Court ruled in February that the president could not use an economic emergency to impose across-the-board tariffs. This time, the administration is relying on Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

Brazil was singled out after trade talks stalled. The plan includes higher taxes on raw and refined sugar and a new 10 percent tariff on aircraft. A senior official described the measures as proposals without strict deadlines, and said the new tariffs would not be added on top of existing duties on cars, steel and aluminum.

The timing is sensitive. A trade truce between Washington and Beijing expires on January 10, and President Trump, who met Chinese leader Xi Jinping last week, plans to host him at the G20 summit in Florida next month. The official said Beijing should not be surprised by the move. Because the United States is one of the world's biggest buyers of foreign goods, any change in its tariffs can ripple through supply chains and consumer prices around the globe.
To sum up, the United States has proposed new tariffs on China and thirteen other trading partners, including South Korea, ahead of key talks with Beijing.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
미국 정부가 새로운 관세를 준비하고 있으며, 한국도 그 대상 경제권에 포함돼 있습니다.
AP 통신에 따르면 트럼프 행정부는 수요일 중국산 상품에 20퍼센트의 추가 관세를 제안했습니다. 이렇게 되면 일부 중국 제품에 붙는 관세는 모두 45퍼센트가 됩니다. 행정부는 또 유럽연합, 일본, 한국, 대만과 다른 주요 교역 상대 9곳에 대한 수입 관세도 올릴 계획입니다.
관리들은 이 조치가 정부 보조금과 무역 장벽 때문에 생긴 과잉 생산을 겨냥한 것이라고 말합니다. 또 지난 2월 대법원이 대통령은 경제 비상사태를 근거로 전면적인 관세를 부과할 수 없다고 판결한 뒤 잃은 세수를 메우려는 목적도 있습니다. 이번에 행정부는 1974년 무역법 301조를 근거로 삼고 있습니다.
브라질은 무역 협상이 교착 상태에 빠진 뒤 따로 지목됐습니다. 계획에는 원당과 정제당에 대한 세금 인상과 항공기에 대한 10퍼센트의 새 관세가 들어 있습니다. 한 고위 관리는 이 조치들이 엄격한 기한이 없는 제안이라고 설명했고, 새 관세는 자동차, 철강, 알루미늄에 붙는 기존 관세에 더해지지 않는다고 말했습니다.

시점이 민감합니다. 미국과 중국의 무역 휴전은 1월 10일에 끝나고, 지난주 시진핑 중국 국가주석을 만난 트럼프 대통령은 다음 달 플로리다에서 열리는 G20 정상회의에 그를 맞이할 계획입니다. 이 관리는 중국이 이번 조치에 놀라지 않을 것이라고 말했습니다. 미국은 세계에서 외국 상품을 가장 많이 사는 나라 중 하나이기 때문에, 미국 관세의 변화는 전 세계 공급망과 소비자 물가에 파급될 수 있습니다.
정리하면, 미국은 중국과의 중요한 협상을 앞두고 중국과 한국을 포함한 다른 교역 상대 13곳에 새 관세를 제안했습니다.

5.headline: Washington Opens a New Front in Its Trade Battles
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Just as the holiday season gets under way in America, Washington has opened a fresh front in its trade battles, and South Korea finds itself in the line of fire.

The Trump administration on Wednesday unveiled plans for an additional 20 percent levy on Chinese imports, a move that, according to the Associated Press, would push the combined duty on some Chinese goods to 45 percent. Higher import taxes are also in store for the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other major trading partners. The proposals were rolled out on the eve of Thanksgiving, after a senior official briefed reporters on condition of anonymity late Tuesday.

The stated rationale is to curb excess manufacturing capacity fueled by subsidies and trade barriers. But the measures serve a second purpose: to recoup revenue lost after the Supreme Court ruled in February that the president could not invoke an economic emergency to impose sweeping, across-the-board tariffs. This time, the administration is leaning on Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, a provision aimed at unfair trade practices.

Brazil, where trade talks have stalled, has been singled out, with steeper taxes on raw and refined sugar and a new 10 percent tariff on aircraft that would weigh on the planemaker Embraer. Officials stressed that the measures remain proposals with no firm timetable, and that they would not stack on top of existing tariffs on autos, steel and aluminum.

The timing could hardly be more delicate. A fragile trade truce between Washington and Beijing is set to expire on January 10. President Trump met Chinese leader Xi Jinping last week and intends to host him at the G20 summit in Florida next month, and the official insisted that Beijing should not be caught off guard. For export-driven economies such as South Korea, the question now is whether these proposals become a bargaining chip or a lasting burden.
To sum up, Washington has proposed a new wave of tariffs targeting China and thirteen other trading partners, setting the stage for tense negotiations in the weeks ahead.
Thank you for listening.

1.headline: London Opens a Very Big New Museum
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
London has a new, very big museum.
It opens this Saturday. It says it is the biggest city museum in the world.
The museum is in old buildings. People sold meat there for hundreds of years.
The museum tells the story of London. The story is about 2,000 years long. It starts with the Romans.
There is a gold coach for a city leader. There is a police box with fish art by Banksy. Banksy is a famous street artist. There is even a piece of a big ball of fat from under the city!
The museum has a mascot. It is a pigeon, a bird you see everywhere in London.
Again, a very big new museum opens in London on Saturday. Thank you for listening.

3.headline: London Opens What It Calls the World's Largest City Museum
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
What do a golden coach, a police box painted by a famous artist and a lump of sewer fat have in common? They are all in a brand-new museum in London.

According to news reports, the London Museum will open its doors this Saturday. It calls itself the largest city museum in the world. The museum is inside old Victorian buildings that were once part of Smithfield, a famous meat market. The project took several years and cost 437 million pounds, or about 573 million dollars.

The new museum replaces the old Museum of London, which closed in 2022. It tells the story of London over about 2,000 years, from the Roman town of Londinium to the Great Fire of 1666 and on to modern times. The museum's director, Sharon Ament, said London has always been a mashup, which means a mix of many different things.

The objects are full of surprises. Visitors can see the Lord Mayor's golden State Coach and a police box that the street artist Banksy decorated with piranhas. There is a piece of the Whitechapel Fatberg, a giant lump of fat and rubbish found in a sewer in 2017. There is also a shirt that King Charles the First may have worn in 1649, the year he died.

Did you know? The meat market at Smithfield has been there for more than 800 years, and it is moving out by 2030. And here is a fun detail: the museum's mascot is a pigeon, a bird you can see all over London.
To sum up, a huge new London Museum opens on Saturday, telling the city's 2,000-year story with some very unusual objects.
Thank you for listening.

알고 계셨나요? 스미스필드 고기 시장은 800년 넘게 그 자리에 있었고, 2030년까지 다른 곳으로 옮겨 갑니다. 재미있는 점이 하나 더 있습니다. 박물관의 마스코트는 런던 어디에서나 볼 수 있는 새, 비둘기입니다.

4.headline: London Museum Opens in a Historic Meat Market
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
A royal coach, a Banksy artwork and a chunk of a notorious sewer blockage are among the treasures waiting for visitors at what is billed as the world's largest city museum.

The London Museum opens on Saturday in a set of Victorian buildings that were once part of Smithfield meat market. According to the Associated Press, the refurbishment took several years and cost 437 million pounds, or about 573 million dollars. The museum replaces the old Museum of London, which stood about half a mile away and closed in 2022.

Its collection traces about 2,000 years of history, from Roman Londinium through the Great Fire of 1666 and the age of empire, to modern movements such as the campaign for women's votes. Director Sharon Ament told reporters that change is the one constant in London, a city she said has always been a mashup.

On the ground floor, the former trading hall, visitors will find the Lord Mayor's State Coach, a telephone switchboard once used at Buckingham Palace, and a police sentry box that Banksy decorated with piranhas in 2024. Other highlights include a piece of the Whitechapel Fatberg, discovered in a sewer in 2017, the bass guitar smashed on the cover of The Clash's album London Calling, and a shirt reputedly worn by King Charles the First at his execution in 1649. A large gallery is devoted to the Cheapside Hoard, a stash of gold and gems found in 1912.

The site has its own history, too. Smithfield has traded meat for more than 800 years, and the market is due to move out by 2030. The museum will keep growing, with underground vaults opening in 2027. Its mascot, fittingly, is a pigeon.
To sum up, London's new museum opens on Saturday in a historic meat market, telling the city's story through some truly unusual objects.
Thank you for listening.

소장품은 로마 시대 론디니움부터 1666년 대화재와 제국 시대를 거쳐 여성 참정권 운동 같은 근현대 운동까지 약 2,000년의 역사를 따라갑니다. 샤론 아멘트 관장은 기자들에게 변화야말로 런던의 유일한 상수이며, 런던은 언제나 '매시업', 즉 뒤섞인 도시였다고 말했습니다.

5.headline: Two Millennia of London History Under One Roof
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Where else could you find a gilded royal carriage, a Banksy police box and a chunk of congealed sewer waste under one roof?

The answer is the new London Museum, which throws open its doors on Saturday and bills itself as the largest city museum in the world. Housed in a cluster of Victorian buildings that once formed part of the Smithfield meat market, the museum is the product of a painstaking, multi-year refurbishment that, according to the Associated Press, carried a price tag of 437 million pounds, roughly 573 million dollars. It supersedes the Museum of London, which sat about half a mile away and shut in 2022.

The galleries chart some 2,000 years of upheaval and reinvention, from Roman Londinium and the Great Fire of 1666 through the imperial era to modern movements ranging from the suffragettes to Black Pride. Director Sharon Ament summed up the spirit of the place neatly, describing change as the city's constant and London itself as a place that has always been a mashup.

The eclectic collection is where the museum truly comes into its own. The former trading hall showcases the Lord Mayor's State Coach alongside a Buckingham Palace telephone switchboard and a police sentry box adorned with piranhas by Banksy. Elsewhere, visitors can marvel at a fragment of the infamous Whitechapel Fatberg, unearthed from a sewer in 2017, the bass guitar Paul Simonon smashed on the cover of London Calling, and the shirt reputedly worn by Charles the First at his execution in 1649. Pride of place goes to the Cheapside Hoard, a trove of seventeenth-century jewels discovered in 1912 that a senior curator likened to a time capsule.

There is a poignant twist, too: Smithfield has hosted a meat market for more than eight centuries, and the traders are due to depart by 2030. The museum, meanwhile, plans to keep expanding, with underground vaults opening in 2027. And in a nod to the city's most ubiquitous resident, its mascot is a pigeon.
To sum up, a vast new London Museum opens on Saturday, weaving two millennia of history into a home carved out of a centuries-old market.
Thank you for listening.

p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

BTS가 찾아오면 무슨 일이 일어날까요? 대만의 한 도시는 도시 전체가 보라색으로 물들었습니다!

이번 투어는 4월에 시작됐습니다. BTS는 이미 북미, 유럽, 남미에서 공연했습니다. 아시아에서는 방콕, 싱가포르, 홍콩 같은 일곱 도시에서 21번의 콘서트를 엽니다. 2월에는 호주에도 갑니다.
가오슝은 그룹을 크게 환영했습니다. 유명한 건물과 강에 보라색 불이 켜졌습니다. 셔틀버스 하나는 BTS가 6월 13일에 데뷔해서 '613번 버스'라는 이름이 붙었습니다. 몇몇 신호등에는 '아미 스톱', '아미 고'라는 글자까지 나왔습니다. 아미는 BTS 팬들의 이름입니다.
공연장에 가지 못한 팬들에게도 기회가 있었습니다. 콘서트 한 편이 80개가 넘는 나라의 영화관에서 상영됐습니다.
정리하면, BTS가 대만에서 아시아 투어를 시작했고 도시는 보라색으로 그룹을 환영했습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: BTS Begins Its Asia-Pacific Tour as Kaohsiung Turns Purple
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
In one city in Taiwan, even the traffic lights changed for BTS. Instead of the usual signs, some street signals said Army Stop and Army Go.

Last week, the K-pop group BTS started the Asia-Pacific part of its Arirang world tour. According to news reports, the first concerts were held at the National Stadium in Kaohsiung, a port city in southern Taiwan. The group played there on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday.

The tour is named after Arirang, the group's fifth full-length album, which came out in March. The tour began in April and has already visited North America, Europe and South America. In Asia, BTS plans 21 concerts in seven cities, including Bangkok, Singapore, Jakarta and Hong Kong. In February, the group will play five more shows in Melbourne and Sydney in Australia.

Kaohsiung welcomed the band in a big way. Famous places, such as the 85 Sky Tower and the Love River, were lit up in purple, the group's special color. A shuttle bus was named Bus 613, because BTS made its debut on June 13. A debut is the first time a singer or group shows its work to the public. And Army is the name of the group's fans, which explains the traffic signals.

Why is this interesting? The Saturday concert was shown live or later in movie theaters in more than 80 countries and regions, on about 3,300 screens. It shows how one K-pop group can bring a whole city, and fans around the world, together.
To sum up, BTS has started the Asian part of its world tour in Taiwan, and the city of Kaohsiung turned purple to welcome it.
Thank you for listening.

정리하면, BTS가 대만에서 월드 투어의 아시아 일정을 시작했고, 가오슝은 보라색으로 물들어 이들을 환영했습니다.

4.headline: BTS Launches Asia-Pacific Leg of Its Arirang World Tour
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
When BTS arrived in Kaohsiung, even the city's pedestrian signals got a makeover, flashing the words Army Stop and Army Go for the group's devoted fans.

The K-pop superstars launched the Asia-Pacific leg of their Arirang world tour last week with three concerts at Kaohsiung National Stadium in southern Taiwan. According to the Korea Herald, the Asian leg includes 21 concerts in seven cities, among them Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Jakarta, Hong Kong and Bulacan in the Philippines. Five more shows in Melbourne and Sydney in February will bring the total for the region to 26 performances in nine cities.

The tour, named after the group's fifth full-length album, released in March, kicked off in April and has already taken BTS across North America, Europe and South America. Its final shows in Brazil wrapped up at the end of October.

Kaohsiung went all out for the occasion. Landmarks such as the 85 Sky Tower, the Love River and the Kaohsiung Music Center were lit in purple, the color closely associated with the band. A shuttle service was branded Bus 613, a nod to the group's debut date of June 13, and a BTS photo zone greeted travelers at the city's international airport.

The excitement is spreading well beyond Taiwan. The second Kaohsiung concert was screened in theaters in more than 80 countries and regions, on roughly 3,300 screens. In Singapore, where BTS will perform four shows in December, a month-long city project is planned, featuring a drone show with about 1,500 drones. Meanwhile, the group was named Most Popular International Artist at Australia's ARIA Awards last week.
To sum up, BTS has opened the Asian leg of its world tour in Taiwan, where an entire city turned purple to welcome the group and its fans.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Kaohsiung Rolls Out the Purple Carpet as BTS Begins Its Asian Swing
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
It is not every day that a city reprograms its traffic lights for a pop band, but that is exactly what greeted BTS fans in Kaohsiung, where pedestrian signals flashed the words Army Stop and Army Go.

The K-pop juggernaut kicked off the Asia-Pacific leg of its Arirang world tour last week with a three-night run at Kaohsiung National Stadium in southern Taiwan. According to the Korea Herald, the Asian swing comprises 21 concerts across seven cities, taking in Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Jakarta, Hong Kong and Bulacan in the Philippines. Add five dates in Melbourne and Sydney next February, and the regional tally climbs to 26 performances in nine cities.

The tour takes its name from Arirang, the group's fifth full-length album, which dropped in March. Since launching in April, the stadium tour has already swept through North America, Europe and South America, wrapping up its Brazilian dates in Sao Paulo at the end of October.

Kaohsiung rolled out the purple carpet. The 85 Sky Tower, the Love River, the Great Harbor Bridge and the Kaohsiung Music Center were all bathed in the band's signature hue, while a shuttle dubbed Bus 613 paid homage to the group's June 13 debut. Musical fountain shows and K-pop random play dance events added to the festival atmosphere, and arriving fans were met by a dedicated photo zone at the international airport.

The buzz is hardly confined to Taiwan. The second Kaohsiung show was beamed to cinemas in more than 80 countries and regions on some 3,300 screens, and Singapore is gearing up for a month-long citywide celebration in December, complete with a light show at Jewel Changi Airport and a 1,500-drone display over Sentosa. The accolades keep piling up, too, with BTS named Most Popular International Artist at Australia's ARIA Awards last week, on top of six trophies, including artist of the year, at this year's Melon Music Awards.
To sum up, BTS has launched the Asian leg of its world tour in Taiwan, turning an entire port city purple and setting the tone for a string of high-profile shows across the region.
Thank you for listening.

K팝의 거물 BTS가 지난주 대만 남부 가오슝 국립경기장에서 사흘 밤 연속 공연을 열며 '아리랑' 월드 투어의 아시아·태평양 일정을 시작했습니다. 코리아헤럴드에 따르면 아시아 일정은 방콕, 쿠알라룸푸르, 싱가포르, 자카르타, 홍콩, 필리핀 불라칸을 거치는 일곱 도시 21회 콘서트로 이뤄집니다. 내년 2월 멜버른과 시드니의 다섯 차례 공연을 더하면 이 지역 공연은 아홉 도시 26회로 늘어납니다.
투어 이름은 3월에 나온 그룹의 다섯 번째 정규 앨범 '아리랑'에서 따왔습니다. 4월에 시작한 이 스타디움 투어는 이미 북미, 유럽, 남미를 휩쓸었고, 10월 말 상파울루에서 브라질 공연을 마무리했습니다.
